summary: Refactored seedLocales() to be idempotent by wrapping each DBHelper::insertDynamic() call with a DBHelper::recordExists() guard for both the locales_application and locales_content tables. Updated PHPDoc to remove the non-idempotency warning and replace it with a description of the existence-check behaviour, consistent with the seedCountries() documentation pattern. All code uses array() syntax throughout. PHP syntax check passes with no errors.

comments.note: seedLocales() and seedCountries() now follow the same idempotency pattern (recordExists guard + conditional insert inside a transaction). The two methods are consistent — no further alignment needed in the files touched.

Once seedLocales() is called during test bootstrap setup these will pass. No action needed within this WP scope.

comments.note: seedLocales() and seedCountries() are now fully aligned on the recordExists-guard pattern. No further alignment needed in TestSuiteBootstrap.php.

Narrow concurrent-call race condition: if two processes pass the recordExists() check simultaneously before either inserts, a duplicate-key exception could still be thrown at the DB level. This is acceptable in seed infrastructure — the Throwable handler rolls back cleanly. Not a production concern.

AppFrameworkTests\Locales\CollectionTest and LanguageTest would directly validate seedLocales() output but require a live seeded test DB. These tests are pre-existing failures unrelated to this WP change, as documented in the implementation pipeline debt comment.
